chunks: And it is narrated from Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from his father, who said:
I saw Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام working in land belonging to him, and his feet had become drenched in sweat. So I said to him, "May I be your ransom, where are the men?"
He said, "O ʿAlī, one better than me and my father worked with his hand in his land."

I said to him, "Who is that?" He said, "The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, the Commander of the Faithful, and my forefathers عليهم السلام. All of them worked with their hands, and this is from the work of the Prophets, the Messengers, and the righteous."

key_terms.أَرْضٍ: land or property in which one personally works
key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.الصَّالِحِينَ: the righteous, whose way includes honest work
key_terms.النَّبِيِّينَ: the Prophets, whose practice is being invoked as precedent
key_terms.الْعَرَقِ: sweat, indicating physical exertion and labor
key_terms.الْمُرْسَلِينَ: the Messengers, included among those who labored
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم as the highest exemplar
key_terms.عَمِلَ بِالْيَدِ: worked with the hand, meaning manual labor and personal effort

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the virtue of working with one’s own hands in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith presents manual labor and working for one’s livelihood as an honorable practice followed by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, and the Imams عليهم السلام. It emphasizes the dignity of personal effort and places such work within the conduct of the Prophets, the Messengers, and the righteous.
